label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: The home page tree opens with a very long accessibility statement text dump before the header and navigation, so the real shop content is buried.
After declining cookies, a second unlabeled-purpose dialog button How can we use your data? and a signup promo popup appeared and stayed in the tree as an open dialog on every page, adding noise.

element.name: How can we use your data?

findings.problem: On arrival the main region was empty with no product list or filters; I had to re-read the page before products appeared, with no loading announcement.
Product page showed raw Liquid error messages and image file names as text in the You May Also Love list, and the main product area was missing at first until re-read.

The color swatches are links named only by an image alt like Captain | Canyon with no indication of which is selected; the header cart link and several other links and buttons have no accessible name.

After pressing Add to cart there was no confirmation message; the button became an unnamed disabled button, and the cart drawer appeared silently. Clicking View cart then timed out although the drawer was open.

The cart drawer has unnamed quantity plus and minus buttons, and the Checkout+ upsell is a pre-promoted paid option; the plain way to continue is a link named Continue without Checkout+ rather than a clear Checkout button.
The checkout page was nearly empty on first load with no loading announcement; the form only appeared after a re-read.
The Package Protection checkbox in the Contact section has no accessible name; its label is a separate strong text, so it is unclear what the checkbox does.
